title: Verifier‑Augmented vs. LLM‑Only NetOps Agents: A Paired Evaluation on an Action‑Aware Staging Benchmark
abstract: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact‑backed paired evaluation comparing a verifier‑augmented NetOps pipeline to an LLM‑only pipeline on ActionAwareStagingBench‑v1. The preregistered design used gpt‑5‑mini as the generator, deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer, N=400 paired tasks (800 episodes), and shared_initial_generation semantics (one LLM candidate per task delivered identically to both conditions). Confirmatory outcomes are exact and deterministic: complete_pairs = 400; baseline_success_count = 400/400; guarded_success_count = 400/400; paired contingency n_11 = 400, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0; observed paired difference = 0.0; preregistered permutation p = 1.0; exact McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples). Diagnostics of provider_call_audit and validator traces show that preregistered shared_initial_generation together with reuse of the same deterministic validator produced a deterministic ceiling that rendered the primary estimand uninformative in this run. We present the preregistered methodology, exact artifact‑grounded results, an artifact‑based operational diagnosis of the ceiling mechanism, and concrete artifact‑grounded recommendations to harden future benchmarks so they expose generator×guard interactions.

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to translate operator intent into network configuration artifacts and staged change workflows (canaries, progressive rollout, rollback). Prior prototype and benchmark studies show LLMs can produce syntactically plausible configuration templates, while separate lines of work demonstrate verifier‑guided generate–validate–repair loops and deterministic network verifiers reduce syntax and semantic errors in IaC and provisioning domains. However, the critical operational question is end‑to‑end: how do generator variability, runtime verification, staged rollout semantics, repair, and rollback interact to determine safe‑deploy outcomes in agentic NetOps pipelines?

Research question and estimand. Under the ActionAwareStagingBench‑v1 semantics used here, does integrating a deterministic runtime validator with an LLM generator increase paired safe‑deploy rate relative to an LLM‑only pipeline? The preregistered primary estimand was the paired difference in safe‑deploy rate (guarded − baseline) measured on N=400 preregistered paired tasks using a paired‑binary confirmatory design.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired evaluation executed with gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with all runtime traces and analysis artifacts archived. (2) Artifact‑grounded confirmatory result: a deterministic ceiling—both conditions achieved 100% safe‑deploy across 400 pairs (paired difference = 0.0; permutation p = 1.0). (3) An evidence‑grounded operational diagnosis of the ceiling (shared per‑pair generation + single deterministic validator used at runtime and for scoring) and a set of concrete, artifact‑implementable hardening recommendations to restore inferential signal in future runs.
sections.related_work: Three literatures frame this study and our recommendations. First, intent→configuration generation: recent work shows feasibility of mapping natural language intent to device configuration (intent‑to‑configuration demonstrations and pretrained/fine‑tuning efforts) but evaluation is often limited to curated corpora or testbeds and generalization remains a challenge (e.g., intent‑based configuration and PreConfig prototypes). Second, verifier‑guided workflows and deterministic verification: studies in IaC and provisioning demonstrate that verifier‑guided training and closed‑loop verifier usage can reduce many classes of configuration errors (TerraFormer and related IaC efforts), while deterministic network verifiers and reachability tools find configuration and policy violations in offline analyses. Third, agentic and tool‑augmented LLM architectures (ReAct, RAG, multi‑agent orchestrations) broaden AIOps capabilities but introduce failure modes—hallucination, misapplied tools, and overconfident outputs—that motivate runtime guardrails and staged deployments. Survey and evaluation‑gap reviews repeatedly call for action‑aware benchmarks combining generation, runtime blocking, staged rollout, repair, rollback, and provenance; our compact ActionAwareStagingBench‑v1 operationalizes those desiderata and exposes a concrete paired‑design pitfall when generation variance is eliminated and scorer invariance is preserved.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered (cnsmauto‑3d2k‑prereg‑v1) as a paired binary confirmatory experiment with exactly N=400 paired tasks and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The planned primary test was a permutation‑based paired difference test, with an exact McNemar test and paired bootstrap CIs prespecified for corroboration.

Execution contract and critical design choices. Execution used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family with declared generator gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as both runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer. The preregistration set shared_initial_generation = true (independent_condition_generation = false): for each task we obtained one LLM candidate and delivered that identical candidate to both baseline and guarded episodes. This choice reduced generator variance intentionally and reduced model‑call budget (model_calls_used = 400 for 800 episodes). The adapter permitted up to one repair call in the guarded episode; repair_applied was recorded (repair_applied = false across episodes).

Task generation, replay, and scoring. Tasks were produced by a seed‑controlled deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 producing structured per‑task difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, pattern, required_command_count, level ∈ {medium, hard, very_hard}). Deterministic replay checks were applied and passed for all pairs. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with full intent‑constraint validation; validator traces record validation_before/after, final_configuration, repair_applied, and validity decisions. All execution and analysis artifacts supporting measurements were archived and used without manual adjudication.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run started 2026‑08‑29T18:23:37Z and completed 2026‑08‑29T19:12:38Z. Planned episodes = 800; completed episodes = 800; failed episodes = 0; model_calls_used = 400 (shared initial generation). Deterministic replay checks passed for all pairs; no exclusions were recorded.

Confirmatory outcomes (artifact‑grounded). The archived confirmatory analysis reports: complete_pairs = 400; baseline_success_count = 400 (baseline_success_rate = 1.0); guarded_success_count = 400 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n_11 = 400 with n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0, yielding observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. The preregistered permutation test returned p = 1.0; the exact McNemar two‑sided test returned p = 1.0; the paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples). Cohen's h = 0.0. These numeric values are reproduced directly from the archived analysis outputs.

Repair, rollback, difficulty distribution, and provider diagnostics. Across all 800 episodes repair_applied = false and no rollbacks were invoked; validator traces show validation_after.final_state matched expected_final_state whenever a candidate was accepted. The archived task manifest yields the difficulty distribution extracted verbatim: medium: 80 tasks (20.0%); hard: 160 tasks (40.0%); very_hard: 160 tasks (40.0%). The deterministic_reconciliation (provider_call_audit) documents hosted_model_call_event_count = 400, cache_miss_count = 400, stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 400}, condition_counts: {shared: 400}, and all deterministic consistency checks passed. Representative validator traces (e.g., task-000001 validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true; repair_applied = false; shared_initial_candidate present) concretely show that each shared candidate was accepted by the deterministic validator and that the same accepted candidate was used to score both baseline and guarded episodes, empirically producing the observed n_11 = 400 contingency.
sections.discussion:
Operational diagnosis: ceiling mechanism. Two preregistered choices caused the deterministic ceiling. First, shared_initial_generation removed generator variance by delivering identical LLM outputs to baseline and guarded episodes. Second, the runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer were the same deterministic implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). When the deterministic validator accepts the shared candidate at runtime, both conditions necessarily record safe‑deploy outcomes and the paired difference is forced to zero. Provider_call_audit records (shared_initial_generation: 400; hosted_model_call_event_count: 400) together with per‑task validator_trace entries (validation_after.valid = true; repair_applied = false) constitute artifact‑level evidence for the causal mechanism that produced the ceiling.

Inference, power, and design lessons. The confirmatory tests correctly report p = 1.0 given the data and the paired bootstrap CI collapses to a point mass at zero. Those inferential outputs are valid but uninformative with respect to generator×guard closed‑loop dynamics because the design prevented the guard from having an opportunity to intervene. The preregistered power rationale assumed a non‑ceiling baseline failure rate; that assumption was falsified by the frozen generator+validator pairing and thus the original power calculation does not apply to this run. The construct validity of the primary estimand requires that generator variance and scorer independence be preserved to allow the guard to alter outcomes.

Artifact‑grounded hardening recommendations. Based on archived manifests and traces, implementable mitigations to restore statistical signal are: (1) independent per‑condition generation (set independent_condition_generation = true) so each condition obtains its own LLM candidate and generator variance can expose guard interventions; (2) use a distinct post‑hoc scorer or a held‑out adjudicator (different implementation or a validator with stochastic perturbation) to avoid conflating runtime blocking and measurement; (3) controlled adversarial seeding to guarantee nontrivial baseline failure rates (select task seeds or perturbations from the archived task manifest that the generator is likely to fail without verifier intervention); (4) difficulty‑stratified sampling: the archived task manifest contains per‑task difficulty labels enabling deterministic stratified resampling to ensure sufficient representation of very_hard tasks; and (5) instrumented mitigation metrics (repair_attempts, repairs_applied, time‑to‑rollback) recorded as explicit numeric outcomes (the validator traces already contain repair_applied and validation timestamps and can be used to compute these metrics). Each recommendation is actionable using artifacts in the archive (task manifest difficulty labels, validator traces, and provider_call_audit logs) and does not require new data or model runs to specify.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired evaluation comparing a verifier‑augmented NetOps pipeline to an LLM‑only pipeline under ActionAwareStagingBench‑v1. Under the preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics and the chosen generator+validator pairing, every shared candidate satisfied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and both conditions produced 100% safe‑deploy across N=400 pairs (paired difference = 0.0; permutation p = 1.0). The deterministic ceiling is a design artifact caused by identical per‑pair generation and reuse of a deterministic validator for runtime blocking and post‑hoc scoring; it renders the primary estimand uninformative for generator×guard closed‑loop interactions in this run. We archive the preregistration and full execution/analysis artifacts to enable reproducibility. The artifact‑grounded hardening recommendations provided here (independent per‑condition generation, distinct scorer, controlled adversarial seeding, difficulty stratification, and mitigation metrics) are concrete steps—directly implementable using the archived task manifest and validator traces—to preserve statistical signal in future evaluations and enable meaningful measurement of blocking, repair, and rollback behaviors.

disclosure_statement: Declared generator: gpt‑5‑mini. Orchestration: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family with shared_initial_generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) as preregistered. Runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: cnsmauto‑3d2k‑prereg‑v1. The immutable initial master prompt is archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. The guarded condition routed the shared LLM candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 which deterministically accepted or blocked candidates per the preregistered adapter policy; the adapter allowed up to one repair call per task but none were applied (repair_applied = false). All runtime calls, raw outputs, validator traces, deterministic replay checks, exclusion logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the artifact bundle and were used without manual adjudication.
limitations: Benchmark hardness and ceiling effect: under preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics and the chosen generator+validator, every shared candidate satisfied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 so the guard had no opportunity to alter outcomes; this makes the primary estimand effectively untestable in this run and invalidates the original power rationale.

Model and scope: the experiment used a single generator (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); results do not generalize across models, validators, or production heterogeneity.

Construct validity: the same deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementation served as both runtime guard and the post‑hoc scorer; this conflation produces concordant acceptance/scoring and limits inference about independent closed‑loop verifier utility.

Shared candidate semantics: preregistered shared_initial_generation (one LLM generation per task shared by both conditions) intentionally reduces generation variance and therefore limits inference to the validator’s behavior on identical candidates rather than full generator+guard closed‑loop interactions.

Synthetic environment and external validity: the simulator and validator do not fully model production telemetry noise, operator workflows, or adversarial actor behaviours; external validity to live networks is limited.

Adversarial robustness untested: adversarial or distribution‑shifted prompts and generator faults that could trigger guard interventions were not exercised in this run and remain open for future work.

Aggregated difficulty reporting: the full per‑task difficulty labels for all N=400 are archived in the task manifest and can be aggregated by auditors; Table 1 reports the artifact‑extracted aggregated counts and percentages.
